notes: Shopify store with Searchspring-powered grids, same site/method as prior Home-Decor pass (notes/39.md). Access: direct HTTP fetch, no blocking; robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (only generic /search disallow, so live site search was not queried, per robots.txt). Navigation discovery: the header nav has a top-level 'NEW' item (secondary-nav, red-highlighted) with an enhanced megamenu 'By Category' section exposing New Furniture, New Decor & Pillows, New Dining, New Pottery, New Lighting, and a 'View All' link to /collections/new-all-new. This is the site's structural 'recently added' merchandising section (equivalent to a New Arrivals / New In / What's New concept) -- not a themed campaign/lookbook: it uses the exact same collection-grid template (ss-collection-snap.js Searchspring integration) as every ordinary category page, with plain category-name children, no editorial copy or seasonal framing, so it was NOT flagged as an ambiguous 'New Collection' page. Checked sitemap_collections_1.xml for additional candidates: found new-by-category-new-art, gifts-by-category-new, new-bath, new-holiday, and several 'new-trending-*' handles (glamtastic, malibu-dreamhouse, outdoor-pillows-rugs, summer-styles, the-kingdom) plus 'ja-newness' and 'newport' -- none of these are linked anywhere in the live header/footer nav (verified against the full homepage HTML), so they are orphaned/past-campaign Shopify collections still indexed by the sitemap but not part of the site's current taxonomy; excluded. 'newport' in particular is a named furniture collection line, not a New Arrivals concept. All qty values captured from the Searchspring search API (bgfilter.collection_handle=<handle> -> pagination.totalResults) and independently cross-verified against Shopify's own /collections/<handle>/products.json unique product-id count for every row below -- all 6 matched exactly. The parent 'New' (all-new, 134) does not equal the sum of the by-category children (21+71+31+59+4=186); this is expected overlap -- the same recently-added product can carry more than one category tag (e.g. a new decor item that is also tagged dining), and/or the parent applies a stricter or differently-windowed 'new' cutoff than the individual category feeds.
